title: Device & Screen
subtitle: A phone in one hand at the net, and the same session on a bigger screen.

hero.alt: TournaQ scoring a live match on a phone

intro: TournaQ is a phone app first, because that is what is actually at the side of a court. Every screen is built for one-handed use, and every scorecard rotates to landscape for a net post or a table.
It works with no signal at all. Data lives on the device, so a beach with no reception is a normal working environment rather than a problem to plan around.
bestfor: Scoring outdoors with one hand and no reception
Propping a phone on a net post in landscape
Long screens — schedules and brackets — on a small display

sections.title: Built for one hand
sections.text: The controls that matter during a rally sit where a thumb reaches, on the device you already have with you.

cards.p: Big targets, the serving side marked, undo within reach. Everything else on the card is secondary to the two buttons you press forty times a set.
cards.alt: The live scorecard on a phone, with large scoring targets

cards.p: Progress, settings and the schedule on one screen, so the organiser's view is a phone screen rather than a spreadsheet.
cards.alt: A session overview on a phone showing progress and the round schedule

cards.p: The whole plan — every round against every court — legible on a phone rather than requiring a laptop.
cards.alt: The court allocation grid on a phone

sections.title: Turn it sideways
sections.text: Every scorecard rotates. In landscape the numbers get bigger and the layout suits a phone propped on a post, where it is read from two metres away rather than held.

cards.p: The same match, laid out for a net post. Nothing is hidden — the layout changes, the functions do not.
cards.alt: A Quick Game scorecard in landscape

cards.p: The court, the score and the controls, sized to be read from the sideline.
cards.alt: A Social Scramble scorecard in landscape

cards.p: Same again under a knockout tie — one layout learned once, used everywhere.

sections.title: When the screen is smaller than the content
sections.text: A fifteen-match schedule or a full bracket is longer than any phone. Rather than shrink it to nothing, TournaQ lets it scroll.

cards.p: Every fixture, every court, every time slot — several screens of it, scrolled rather than squeezed. The same page on a tablet simply shows more of it at once.
cards.alt: A full league fixture list, several phone screens long

cards.h: A bracket that pans and zooms
cards.p: Brackets and crosstables get their own canvas: pinch to zoom, drag to pan, and tap a team to trace its path. A structure that needs width gets width, instead of being folded into a list.
cards.alt: An elimination bracket on a pan-and-zoom canvas

sections.title: No signal, no account
sections.text: Everything above works with the phone in aeroplane mode. That is a design decision, not a limitation.

cards.p: Tournaments, players and results are stored locally. There is no sign-up, no sync to wait for and nothing to lose when the reception goes — which on a beach it will.
cards.alt: The TournaQ home screen on a phone

cards.p: When something does need to move, it moves directly: a QR code between two phones, or an exported file. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
cards.alt: A QR code sheet for handing a scorecard to another device

feature_list_text: Phone support ships today. Dedicated large-screen and cast-to-display layouts are on the way.
feedback: Using TournaQ on a device that does not suit it? Tell us what you are running it on.
